text:
deploy-bot: Scheduled rollout for customer `dynamo-fin` in Dedicated.
- Release: v2.3.1 (model) -> runtime 1.4.0
- Change window: 2026-04-02 22:00 UTC to 2026-04-03 02:00 UTC
- Canary plan: 5% for 20m (manual approval) -> 50% for 30m -> 100%
- Rollback thresholds: p95 latency increase > 80ms OR error rate > 1.5% sustained for 5m
- Pin strategy: pin customer to v2.3.1 during rollout; automatic unpin only after full success
- Links: https://console.redwood/internal/rollouts/rollout-12345

sara liu: Ack. 22:00 UTC is fine from customer side. Dynamo asked for a short canary (20m) then faster ramp.

mike ryan: I'm infra oncall for the window. I'll monitor GPU utilization and autoscaler. Quick Q: who will run the manual approval after the 5% hold?

anika patel: Product/CS will standby for smoke validation. If infra + ops give green, I can click approve. Also, please confirm KV cache warm plan.

oliver chen: Artifact validated in staging. sha256: `abc123def4567890...` Tests: 128/128 pass. I'll execute cache pre-warm script ~10m before cutoff.

release-manager: Notes for the approver:
1) Verify artifact checksum matches the one in the release notes.
2) Run these smoke prompts against the canary endpoint: `{"prompts":["account balance","recent transactions"]}`
3) Watch the eval dashboard for quality regressions (confidence drop or hallucination rate).

oncall-bot: Reminder: automatic monitoring hook will post alerts to #incidents and trigger pager if rollback threshold breached.

mike ryan: Proposed manual rollback command if needed:
```
./releasectl rollback --customer dynamo-fin --to-version v2.2.8 --reason "latency regression"
```
I'll be ready to run it; team please confirm ownership.

anika patel: Ops will own the approval click, infra runs the rollback command if we get alerts.

release-manager: Canary config (to be applied by release system):
```json
{
  "customer": "dynamo-fin",
  "steps": [
    {"pct": 5, "hold_mins": 20, "manual_approval": true},
    {"pct": 50, "hold_mins": 30, "manual_approval": false},
    {"pct": 100, "hold_mins": 0, "manual_approval": false}
  ],
  "rollback_triggers": {
    "latency_p95_ms": 80,
    "error_rate_pct": 1.5
  }
}
```

oliver chen: Will post the exact pre-warm command ~1h before deploy. Also adding a quick smoke harness in case we need a rollback power-check.

sara liu: +1 from Dynamo on the plan. They want a short post-rollout verification period before we close the change ticket.

release-manager: Last checklist before window:
- [x] Artifact checksum verified (oliver)
- [x] Staging tests passed (oliver)
- [x] Oncall coverage confirmed (mike)
- [x] CS/product approval for customer (sara/anika)
- [ ] Post-rollout verification script ready (oliver)

mike ryan: I'll be online for the full window. If we see anything borderline, prefer rollback. No risky DB changes in this release so rollback is just a version pin revert.

anika patel: Approved from my side. I'll hit the manual approval after the 5% hold if dashboards look green.

sara liu: :thumbsup: Dynamo confirms go for 22:00 UTC.

deploy-bot: Rollout job queued. Reminder: after full success, the system will automatically unpin after 24h unless the customer requests otherwise.

release-manager: Merging to ops runbook: we will start canary at 22:00, hold 20m, then escalate per plan. Any last blockers?

oliver chen: none from infra. Posting pre-warm now: `curl -sX POST https://internal/edge/warm -d '{"customer":"dynamo-fin","keys":["prompt:balance","prompt:tx:recent"]}'`

mike ryan: Ready.

anika patel: Approved. Proceed when you see green after 5% hold.

sara liu: Thanks all, passing along to Dynamo engagement lead.

oncall-bot: If rollback is executed, create incident with tag `dynamo-rollout` and link to rollout job.
